key_insight: Scaling Representation Autoencoder (RAE) decoders on a frozen high-quality encoder (SigLIP-2) for text-to-image generation improves overall image fidelity, but careful dataset composition (web, synthetic, text-rendered) is still crucial for reliable text conditioning and compositional control.
problem_solved: Enables scaling RAE-based diffusion models from ImageNet to open-ended text-to-image generation while maintaining high fidelity and semantic alignment, addressing whether semantic latent RAEs can generalize to large-scale, freeform T2I tasks.
method: Freeze a pre-trained representation encoder (SigLIP-2) and scale RAE decoders trained in a high-dimensional semantic latent space.
Train on a mixture of web images, synthetic data, and text-rendered examples to improve generalization to freeform captions.
Use diffusion transformers operating in the RAE latent space to generate images conditioned on text.
impact: Shows a practical path to scale semantic-latent diffusion for high-quality, controllable T2I models while leveraging a frozen encoder—reducing retraining cost and focusing engineering effort on decoder scaling and dataset design.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: frozen SigLIP-2 encoder -> RAE latent space -> scaled diffusion transformer decoder
Dataset composition chart: proportions of web / synthetic / text-rendered data and their effect on metrics
Scaling curve: image fidelity (or FID/CLIP-score) vs. decoder scale and vs. dataset scale
Qualitative grid: generated images with corresponding captions highlighting improvements and failure modes
paper_title: Scaling Text-to-Image Diffusion Transformers with Representation Autoencoders
paper_authors: Shengbang Tong, Boyang Zheng, Ziteng Wang, Bingda Tang, Nanye Ma
